author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The silent drop of scan lines from the northern stores last night exposed a critical gap in our ingestion flow. The model forecasted zero demand for fresh produce because the data simply did not arrive. I am not willing to let the hand-over from ingestion to validation proceed without a formal review step. A manual check is not enough to guarantee that every store's data arrives on time and in complete form. If we skip this review, the risk of another silent failure remains too high. I need a hard stop in the pipeline that forces a validation check before any data is pushed to the feature store. This is non-negotiable for the reliability of the morning order window. We cannot trust the forecast if the input data is incomplete, and I will not sign off on a process that lacks this protective gate.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they will not sign off on a process without a mandatory validation gate, establishing a strict limit that crossing it constitutes a refusal of their acceptance.
